gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two roughly $135 front-only 4K cameras differ about 2x in data per frame and hours per card (VIOFO A119M Pro 62.0 Mb/s = 27.9 GB/h = 4.6 h per 128 GB; Vantrue S1 Pro Max 1CH 32.0 Mb/s = 14.4 GB/h = 8.9 h per 128 GB), or what is left of $200 once each camera has its maker's hardwire kit.
standout_why: Compared against roadgearlab.com (cited), productbible.com (cited), tonyreviewsthings.com, pacificpartsdept.com and Dealectric's own front-and-rear page; caranddriver.com could not be fetched. RoadGearLab already derives GB per hour and hours per 256 GB card for the A119M Pro (~28 GB/h, ~9.2 h) and the 70mai A810S (~18 GB/h, ~14.4 h), and gives a general pixels-per-degree figure (4K over 125 degrees, about 31). Product Bible already totals camera plus a 128 GB card (A119M Pro $169.98) and says a kit and card add about $55 to $65. What they lack: any figure for the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (neither page names it), bits per pixel, per-camera pixels per degree, and a camera plus hardwire-kit total set against the $200 cap.
decides: It confirms the VIOFO A119M Pro as the front-only detail pick (most data per 4K frame, 0.249 bit per pixel), but only at Amazon's $132.99; VIOFO's own store reads $209.99 today, over the cap. Among cameras we can link, the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 1CH ($135.99 at vantrue.com, partner store, no record yet) is the 1-channel 4K row that fits: about twice the hours per card at about half the data per frame, and DashCamTalk scores the S1 Pro Max 6.8 against the A119M Pro's 7.8. The S1 Pro Max 4K + 2.5K at $199.99 leaves $0.01 of the budget for a card or hardwire kit. Two flags to settle before our rows go in: DDPAI's store search read $259.00 for the N5 Pro today (our record has $179.00 from 11-17), and Vortex Radar calls the multi-camera Botslab G980H's 2160p mode 'fake 4K' from a 5 MP sensor.

findings.note: Read through viofo.com's store search feed (storecheck search), in stock, no compare-at price; the product page itself returned HTTP 429, so variants were not read. $209.99 - $200 = $9.99 over the cap. 1-channel (front only), 3840x2160, Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678, 140-degree lens, microSD up to 512 GB, CPL filter in the box, all per the listing text.

findings.label: Other sellers' prices, as tracked by DashCamTalk
findings.note: DashCamTalk's price table dated Nov 26, 2026. The Amazon listing itself was not opened. Under $200 only away from VIOFO's own store. ChatGPT's two chats showed Best Buy at $139.99 and then $189.99.

findings.label: Front 4K bitrate and storage per hour
findings.note: DashCamTalk spec table: 3840x2160 at 30 fps, 62.0 Mbps, 140 degrees, capacitor, GPS, score 7.8/10. Arithmetic: 62.0 x 3600 / 8 / 1000 = 27.9 GB/h. It is a spec-table figure, not a file measurement.

findings.label: Hours of 4K before the loop overwrites
findings.value: about 4.6 h on 128 GB, 9.2 h on 256 GB, 18.4 h on 512 GB (its maximum)
findings.note: 128 / 27.9 = 4.6; 256 / 27.9 = 9.2; 512 / 27.9 = 18.4. Uses nominal card size; formatted capacity and locked event clips shorten it. RoadGearLab already prints the 256 GB figure.

findings.label: Data per 4K frame
findings.note: 62,000,000 / (3840 x 2160 x 30) = 0.249. That is 1.94x the Vantrue S1 Pro Max front (62.0 / 32.0) and 2.11x the 70mai A810S front (62.0 / 29.4).

findings.label: Pixels per degree of stated lens angle, 4K front
findings.value: A119M Pro 27.4; A810S 26.3; S1 Pro Max 24.8 px per degree
findings.note: 3840 / 140 = 27.4 (angle from viofo.com); 3840 / 146 = 26.3 (DashCamTalk); 3840 / 155 = 24.8 (vantrue.com and DashCamTalk). A 12-inch plate at 30 ft spans 1.91 degrees, so about 52, 50 and 47 pixels. Treats the stated angle as horizontal with even spread, the same method RoadGearLab uses; no source read says whether these angles are diagonal, so use it for ranking only. The spread is about 10%, too small to decide the pick alone.
